Case Diary is perused.
Learned counsel for the rival parties are heard.
The petitioner has filed this first application u/S 438 Cr.P.C. for grant of anticipatory bail.

Petitioner apprehends arrest in connection with offences punishable u/Ss. 270, 272, 273, 420 of IPC r/w 57, 59, 63, 64 of Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006 registered as Crime No.1132/18 at Police Station City Kotwali District Morena.

entities.text: Police Station City Kotwali District Morena
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Learned Public Prosecutor for the State opposed the application and prayed for its rejection by contending that on the basis of the allegations and the material available on record, no case for grant of anticipatory bail is made out.

Petitioner is apprehending arrest in regard to allegation that he alongwith the other co-accused was preparing adulterated paneer in their factory where ingredients for preparing adulterated paneer have been recovered.
The offences alleged against the petitioner are u/S. 270, 272 and 273 of IPC are all bailable though cognizable.
The other offences alleged are punishable u/S. 57, 59, 63 and 64 of Food Safety and Standard Act which do not prescribe punishment for more than six months.
However, the State has also alleged the offence of cheating punishable u/S. 420 of IPC which attracts punishment of imprisonment upto seven years.

In the prima facie opinion of this court, though the offence of cheating does not appear to be made out but the matter deserves deeper probe and therefore, liberty is granted to the State to argue on the said issue by bringing relevant citation and supportive material.
The allegation against the petitioner is of serious nature which has potentiality of adversely affecting the health of a large number of persons.

However, it seems that due to law not prescribing higher Arif Khan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 30 November, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138611153/
1 punishment for such offences which adversely affect the society at large, petitioner appears to be taking advantage of the vacuum in law.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the State has cited decision of the Apex Court in the case of Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre vs. State of Maharashtra and Others 2011 (1) SCC 694 Para 112 to emphasize the relevant consideration which should weigh in the mind of the court while considering the application for anticipatory bail.

entities.text: Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre vs. State of Maharashtra and Others 2011 (1) SCC 694 Para 112
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Despite the offences involving insignificant punishment, this court is of the considered view that deeper probe is required in the matter and therefore, the matter be listed on 4th December, 2018 for the State to argue on the issue as to whether the offence u/S. 420 of IPC would be attracted or not.
This court meanwhile is inclined to extend the benefit of anticipatory bail to the petitioner but with certain stringent conditions.

Accordingly, without expressing opinion on merits of the case, this application u/S 438 Cr.P.C is allowed and it is hereby directed that in the event of arrest, the petitioner shall be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in sum of Rs. 1,00,000/- (Rs. One Lac Only) with two solvent sureties each of Rs. 50,000/-to the satisfaction of Arresting Authority.

This order shall remain operative subject to compliance of the following conditions by the petitioner :-
1.

The petitioner shall comply with all the terms and conditions of the bond executed by him;
2. The petitioner shall cooperate in the investigation/trial, as the case may be;

The petitioner shall not seek unnecessary adjournments during the trial; and 6. The petitioner shall not leave India without previous permission of the trial Court/Investigating Officer, as the case may be.
7. The petitioner shall mark his presence at the concerned police station every day between 10 am to 11 am till the next date of hearing.
